note: Everyday topics added by hand on 14 Oct 2026 to fill gaps found by retrieval test 1. 'in_sample' marks additions that touch one of the 20 tuning questions (overfitting risk). Terms that appear in the 10 held-out questions (herd immunity, vaccination, tsunami, drones, drug funding, grading, interest rates, central bank, inflation, Māori land, proof, primes, colonisation, language models in CS.K4) were deliberately removed from curated lists so the held-out test stays clean.

additions.statement: AI and agent security covers attacks on, and safeguards for, language models and autonomous software agents.
Generative AI covers language and image models that produce new content and act as software agents.
Medicines regulation states how the state approves, licenses and monitors drugs and therapeutic products.
leaves: Medsafe, the New Zealand medicines regulator

additions.statement: Labour markets settle the allocation of work through wages, hiring and bargaining between workers and employers.
Civil structures are designed fixed systems whose behaviour is set by loads, ground conditions and earthquake shaking.
Histories of war and conflict assert that wars, their causes and their conduct shaped what happened.
Metaphysics of the person and agency asks whether we act freely and what makes us the same person over time.
Normative ethics asks which general theory explains why acts are right or wrong.
World religions are the major living traditions, each with its own account of the ultimate.
Worship and ritual are the acts through which believers express and enact their faith together.
Proof and the foundations of mathematics ask what a valid proof is and what axioms mathematics rests on.
Everyday discrete mathematics studies primes, networks and counting problems met outside pure research.
Contemporary security problems are the strategic settings of deterrence, cyber conflict and irregular war.
Product and visual design disciplines shape everyday objects, garments and graphics for use.
Inclusive design responds to the needs of people with different abilities, ages and cultures.
Literary genres are the familiar forms in which written works are composed and read.
Common themes are the recurring subjects, such as love, death and identity, that works explore.
Elections and voting cover how citizens choose representatives and how electoral rules shape the result.
leaves: Electoral systems, including MMP and proportional representation

additions.statement: Everyday legal processes are the routine ways ordinary people use the law to resolve matters.
